With user switching enabled as a username + password combo, I was able to login to the root account from the login screen with no password on 10.13.1. It's not just a UI bug, it's a full on authentication bypass.

Can this be used remotely? Edit: Yes, after turning on Remote Management on my second mac I was able to log into it using Remote Desktop, account root and no pw. It only works after getting physical access once.
Fix this by setting a password for root (or disable). Instructions here: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204012
Confirmed on 10.13.1. As a workaround, once you login as 'root', you can change the password to something else, and the empty password will stop working.
Apple's window management has always sucked... Into the 2000s, the only way you could resize a window on the Mac was to drag its lower-right corner. That is it. NO other corner, and no edge.
Tahoe is a macOS mis-step on par with Windows 8 or Windows Vista... my feedback is pretty succinct: 'I don't recommend others upgrade. I wish I didn't.'
After using Tahoe for a week, I've found I leave it in my bag. Window operations are painful and it feels like a bad try at a tablet os without a stylus or touch screen.
I have been using Moom for a long time for moving windows without holding from any particular position and resizing windows without grabbing a particular corner. Life changing small things.
This behavior is similar to Windows 11. You have to position the mouse just outside the window. It is non-intuitive and awful. These are problems humanity solved over 35 years ago (see NeXTSTEP).
macOS sends hashes of every opened executable to some server of theirs and when trustd and syspolicyd are unable to do so, the entire operating system grinds to a halt.

My MacBook is basically unusable right now... how can you allow this to happen? Your services hanging should never prevent my device from running things locally. This is seriously making me reconsider my next computer purchase.
Adding: 0.0.0.0 ocsp.apple.com to /private/etc/hosts solves it. Can't believe Big Sur is somehow affecting my Mohave Mac! Yikes!
Champions of privacy, phoning home a hash of every executable your computer runs!
pbcopy and pbpaste are one of my most-loved in the list. Dealing with some minified json, switching to iTerm, doing pbpaste | json_pp | pbcopy and having a clean output is so nice.
networkQuality is something I really wish I knew about sooner. A good replacement for opening up Speedtest or whatnot when you just want to figure out if the network is slow.

fs_usage is easily one of the most useful of them all... I can't count the number of times a bit of fs_usage foo has helped me dig out of a seriously messy pile of network, file and page fault issues.
Apple's most recent OS where it appears that low-level system API such as exec and getxattr now do synchronous network activity before returning to the caller.

I can run 'terraform apply' and it could take up to 5 minutes to start, leaving my computer almost unusable until it runs. It's already been a few months since I try to run every command from a VM in a remote location.

Increasingly I find macOS only to be tolerable with iCloud (and Siri, location, suggestions, bug reporting, etc) entirely disabled... It phones home constantly even with all of the services disabled/opted out.
